#!/usr/bin/env sh
# download_run.sh — host-side cron entry for one climate_download job.
#
# The HOST decides which init to fetch and passes --date/--cycle explicitly, so:
#   * the container's timezone / clock is irrelevant (we trust only the host clock);
#   * the *_ser.yaml never pins a date, so a historical backfill running inside
#     the container can't collide with the operational schedule.
#
# It runs the job *inside the long-running dev container* (`zhangmy-dev`),
# writing per-step GRIB subsets + a per-init manifest.json under /climate_data.
# The restore side (climate_restorage/deploy/restore_scan.sh) slices each new
# manifest to Zarr on its next tick — the manifest is the only cross-component
# signal, so the two cron schedules need no coordination.
#
# Usage (from cron):
#   download_run.sh <job-yaml> [extra climate_download args...]
#
# Backfill a specific init (skips the host date computation):
#   INIT_DATE=20260701 CYCLE=12 download_run.sh <job-yaml>
#
# Example crontab line (times are CHINA local — see deploy/README.md):
#   30 2 * * *  /srv/climate/download_run.sh config/jobs/gfs_renewables_ser.yaml >> /var/log/climate/download_gfs.log 2>&1
set -eu

JOB="${1:?usage: download_run.sh <job-yaml> [extra climate_download args...]}"
shift

CONTAINER="${CONTAINER:-zhangmy-dev}"
DOWNLOAD_DIR="${DOWNLOAD_DIR:-/workspace/climate_down}"
CYCLE="${CYCLE:-12}"                       # which forecast cycle (UTC hour)
PUBLISH_LAG_HOURS="${PUBLISH_LAG_HOURS:-5}" # hrs after CYCLE:00 UTC when the run is fully out

# --- Decide the init date(s) on the HOST --------------------------------------
# Pick the most recent <cycle>z run that has already published: shift "now" back
# by (cycle + lag) hours and take that UTC date. This is robust to WHEN the cron
# fires — it always resolves to the latest available <cycle>z, so the exact cron
# time stops being critical (a late/extra run just re-resolves and resumes).
#
# LOOKBACK_DAYS>0 also re-verifies the previous N days' <cycle>z in the same run
# (as a date RANGE, which climate_download expands init-by-init). Combined with
# per-step resume this is a cheap self-heal: a run interrupted on an earlier day
# (container restart / network drop, no manifest written) is completed by the
# next day's run instead of being stranded. Complete inits skip in milliseconds.
if [ -n "${INIT_DATE:-}" ]; then
  DATE="$INIT_DATE"                        # explicit override (backfill)
else
  BACK=$(( CYCLE + PUBLISH_LAG_HOURS ))
  # GNU date (Linux host). BSD/macOS host: use `date -u -v-"${BACK}"H +%Y%m%d`.
  END=$(date -u -d "${BACK} hours ago" +%Y%m%d)
  if [ "${LOOKBACK_DAYS:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    START=$(date -u -d "$(( BACK + LOOKBACK_DAYS * 24 )) hours ago" +%Y%m%d)
    DATE="${START}-${END}"                 # range: re-verify recent inits + latest
  else
    DATE="$END"
  fi
fi

NAME="$(basename "$JOB" .yaml)_${CYCLE}z"
LOCK="${LOCK:-/home/zhangmingyu/operation/lock/download_${NAME}.lock}"   # ON THE HOST

# flock creates the lock FILE but not its parent dir — ensure the dir exists on
# the host so a custom LOCK path doesn't fail with "No such file or directory".
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOCK")"

# Container down -> clean skip (exit 0); the next run resumes, losing nothing.
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx "$CONTAINER"; then
  echo "download_run: container '$CONTAINER' not running; skipping $NAME." >&2
  exit 0
fi

echo "download_run: $NAME -> init ${DATE} ${CYCLE}z (host-computed UTC)"

# flock -n -E 0 ON THE HOST: if a previous run of THIS (job, cycle) is still
# going, exit 0 instead of stacking a second downloader on the same init.
# (-E needs util-linux >= 2.27 on the HOST; drop it if the host's flock is older.)
rc=0
flock -n -E 0 "$LOCK" \
  docker exec -w "$DOWNLOAD_DIR" "$CONTAINER" \
    uv run climate_download run --config "$JOB" \
      --date "$DATE" --cycle "$CYCLE" --no-progress "$@" \
  || rc=$?

# climate_download exit codes: 0 all-ok, 1 partial, 2 all-failed.
# Partial is usually benign (a step not yet published) — log it but do not fail
# the cron line, so monitoring only alerts on a true all-failed run.
case "$rc" in
  0) echo "download_run: $NAME OK" ;;
  1) echo "download_run: $NAME PARTIAL (some steps missing/failed — often a late publish; a later run fills them)" >&2; rc=0 ;;
  2) echo "download_run: $NAME ALL-FAILED — investigate (upstream outage? disk full?)" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "download_run: $NAME exited $rc" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$rc"

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# restore_scan.sh — host-side cron entry for the climate_restore slicing step.
#
# Structure mirrors download/deploy/download_run.sh: the HOST cron drives the
# long-running dev container (`zhangmy-dev`) via `docker exec`. The one difference
# from a plain container job is the lock placement:
#
#   host crontab -> flock (lock ON THE HOST) -> docker exec zhangmy-dev -> scan-once
#
# i.e. flock wraps `docker exec` on the host side, so the lock file lives on the
# host — not inside the container. This keeps overlapping cron ticks from stacking
# two scans while the host `docker exec` client is alive (it stays attached until
# the in-container run exits). scan-once is idempotent anyway, so the lock is a
# resource guard, not a correctness requirement.
#
# It idempotently sweeps every *.manifest.json under DATA_ROOT (inside the
# container) and turns each finished init into a per-source Zarr store. Re-runs are
# cheap: already-built outputs are skipped (keyed off the on-disk .zarr).
#
# Install (host crontab), every 10 minutes:
#   */10 * * * * /srv/climate/restore_scan.sh >> /var/log/climate/restore_scan.log 2>&1
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - the dev container is running and stays up (cron drives it via `docker exec`)
#   - the cron user can run docker (in the `docker` group or root)
#   - restore deps synced once inside it:
#       docker exec -w /workspace/climate_restorage zhangmy-dev uv sync
#
# Any value below can be overridden from the environment if your layout differs.
set -eu

CONTAINER="${CONTAINER:-zhangmy-dev}"
RESTORE_DIR="${RESTORE_DIR:-/workspace/climate_restorage}"        # inside the container
DATA_ROOT="${DATA_ROOT:-/climate_data}"                           # inside: common parent of all sources
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-/climate_data/climate_data_storage/zarr}"     # inside the container
JOB="${JOB:-config/jobs/gfs_zarr_china.yaml}"                     # relative to RESTORE_DIR (inside)
SOURCE="${SOURCE:-gfs-0p25}"                        # empty = scan all sources; e.g. gfs-0p25 to scope one
LOCK="${LOCK:-/home/zhangmingyu/operation/lock/restore_scan.lock}"      # ON THE HOST (flock runs host-side, see below)

# flock creates the lock FILE but not its parent dir — ensure the dir exists on
# the host so a custom LOCK path (e.g. /home/<user>/operation/restore_scan.lock)
# doesn't fail with "No such file or directory".
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOCK")"

# Container down -> clean skip (exit 0); the next tick resumes, losing nothing.
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx "$CONTAINER"; then
  echo "restore_scan: container '$CONTAINER' not running; skipping this tick." >&2
  exit 0
fi

SRC_ARG=""
[ -n "$SOURCE" ] && SRC_ARG="--source $SOURCE"

# flock -n -E 0 ON THE HOST: if a previous scan is still running, exit 0 instead
# of stacking a second one (two in-place .zarr rewrites of one init would corrupt
# it). `-E 0` needs util-linux >= 2.27 on the HOST; drop it if the host's flock is
# older.
rc=0
flock -n -E 0 "$LOCK" \
  docker exec -w "$RESTORE_DIR" "$CONTAINER" \
    uv run climate_restore scan-once \
      --download-root "$DATA_ROOT" \
      --output-dir    "$OUT_DIR" \
      --output-format zarr \
      $SRC_ARG \
      --config "$JOB" \
  || rc=$?

# scan-once exit codes: 0 = all processed/skipped (incl. container down or lock
# held by a concurrent run), 1 = at least one *ready* manifest failed to process.
case "$rc" in
  0) echo "restore_scan: OK" ;;
  1) echo "restore_scan: FAILED — a ready manifest failed to process; check the log" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "restore_scan: exited $rc" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$rc"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reconcile recent production NWP initializations on the host."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import fcntl
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import NamedTuple


class SourcePolicy(NamedTuple):
    source: str
    job: str
    cycle: int
    publish_lag_hours: int
    lookback_days: int
    expected_steps: tuple[int, ...]
    log_name: str


DWD_STEPS = tuple(range(0, 79)) + tuple(range(81, 181, 3))
GFS_STEPS = tuple(range(0, 121)) + tuple(range(123, 385, 3))
IFS_STEPS = tuple(range(0, 145, 3)) + tuple(range(150, 361, 6))
AIFS_STEPS = tuple(range(0, 361, 6))

POLICIES = (
    SourcePolicy("dwd-icon", "config/jobs/dwd-icon_renewables_ser.yaml", 12, 5, 0, DWD_STEPS, "download_icon.log"),
    SourcePolicy("dwd-icon", "config/jobs/dwd-icon_renewables_ser.yaml", 0, 3, 0, DWD_STEPS, "download_icon_00z.log"),
    SourcePolicy("gfs-0p25", "config/jobs/gfs_renewables_ser.yaml", 12, 5, 2, GFS_STEPS, "download_gfs.log"),
    SourcePolicy("aifs-single", "config/jobs/aifs_renewables_ser.yaml", 12, 6, 2, AIFS_STEPS, "download_aifs.log"),
    SourcePolicy("ifs-hres", "config/jobs/ifs_renewables_ser.yaml", 12, 8, 2, IFS_STEPS, "download_ifs.log"),
    SourcePolicy("ifs-hres", "config/jobs/ifs_renewables_ser.yaml", 0, 8, 2, IFS_STEPS, "download_ifs_00z.log"),
)


def latest_init_date(now: datetime, policy: SourcePolicy) -> str:
    """Return the newest init expected to be fully published at *now*."""

    shifted = now.astimezone(timezone.utc) - timedelta(
        hours=policy.cycle + policy.publish_lag_hours
    )
    return shifted.strftime("%Y%m%d")


def candidate_dates(now: datetime, policy: SourcePolicy) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return recent init dates from oldest to newest for one policy."""

    latest = datetime.strptime(latest_init_date(now, policy), "%Y%m%d")
    return tuple(
        (latest - timedelta(days=days_ago)).strftime("%Y%m%d")
        for days_ago in range(policy.lookback_days, -1, -1)
    )


def _raw_path(path_value: str, data_root: Path, manifest: Path) -> Path:
    path = Path(path_value)
    try:
        relative = path.relative_to("/climate_data")
    except ValueError:
        return path if path.is_absolute() else manifest.parent / path
    return data_root / relative


def manifest_health(
    manifest: Path,
    data_root: Path,
    expected_steps: int | Sequence[int],
    *,
    verify_boundaries: bool = False,
) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Validate the ready signal, step set and raw-file sizes.

    Boundary reads are opt-in because a kernel-level storage wait can otherwise
    pin the periodic reconciler in uninterruptible I/O indefinitely.
    """

    if not manifest.is_file():
        return False, "manifest missing"
    try:
        payload = json.loads(manifest.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        return False, f"manifest unreadable: {exc}"
    if not payload.get("completed_at"):
        return False, "manifest has no completed_at"
    failures = payload.get("failures") or []
    if failures:
        return False, f"manifest has {len(failures)} failure(s)"
    files = payload.get("files") or []
    steps = [entry.get("step_hours") for entry in files]
    if len(steps) != len(set(steps)):
        return False, "manifest has duplicate steps"
    if isinstance(expected_steps, int):
        if len(steps) != expected_steps:
            return False, f"manifest has {len(steps)}/{expected_steps} steps"
    elif set(steps) != set(expected_steps):
        return False, f"manifest step set differs ({len(steps)}/{len(expected_steps)})"
    for entry in files:
        raw = _raw_path(str(entry.get("path", "")), data_root, manifest)
        try:
            if raw.stat().st_size != int(entry["size_bytes"]):
                return False, f"size mismatch: {raw.name}"
            if verify_boundaries:
                with raw.open("rb", buffering=0) as handle:
                    if handle.read(4) != b"GRIB":
                        return False, f"invalid GRIB boundary: {raw.name}"
                    handle.seek(-4, 2)
                    if handle.read(4) != b"7777":
                        return False, f"invalid GRIB boundary: {raw.name}"
        except (OSError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return False, f"raw file missing or unreadable: {raw.name}"
    return True, "complete"


def manifest_path(data_root: Path, policy: SourcePolicy, date: str) -> Path:
    cycle = f"{policy.cycle:02d}z"
    return data_root / policy.source / date / cycle / f"{date}_{cycle}_{policy.source}.manifest.json"


def _parse_now(value: str | None) -> datetime:
    if value is None:
        return datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))


def _selected_policies(only: set[str], excluded: set[str]) -> tuple[SourcePolicy, ...]:
    return tuple(
        policy
        for policy in POLICIES
        if (not only or policy.source in only) and policy.source not in excluded
    )


def reconcile(
    *,
    now: datetime,
    data_root: Path,
    runner: Path,
    log_dir: Path,
    policies: Sequence[SourcePolicy],
    dry_run: bool,
    verify_boundaries: bool,
) -> int:
    unresolved = 0
    for policy in policies:
        for date in candidate_dates(now, policy):
            manifest = manifest_path(data_root, policy, date)
            healthy, reason = manifest_health(
                manifest,
                data_root,
                policy.expected_steps,
                verify_boundaries=verify_boundaries,
            )
            label = f"{policy.source} {date} {policy.cycle:02d}z"
            if healthy:
                print(f"HEALTHY {label}")
                continue
            print(f"REPAIR {label}: {reason}")
            if dry_run:
                continue
            log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            environment = os.environ.copy()
            environment.update(
                INIT_DATE=date,
                CYCLE=str(policy.cycle),
                PUBLISH_LAG_HOURS=str(policy.publish_lag_hours),
            )
            log_path = log_dir / policy.log_name
            try:
                with log_path.open("a") as log:
                    log.write(f"\n# reconcile_sources: {label} ({reason})\n")
                    log.flush()
                    result = subprocess.run(
                        [str(runner), policy.job],
                        env=environment,
                        stdout=log,
                        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                        check=False,
                    )
            except OSError as exc:
                print(f"UNRESOLVED {label}: runner failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
                unresolved += 1
                continue
            healthy, reason = manifest_health(
                manifest,
                data_root,
                policy.expected_steps,
                verify_boundaries=verify_boundaries,
            )
            if result.returncode != 0 or not healthy:
                print(
                    f"UNRESOLVED {label}: runner rc={result.returncode}; {reason}",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                unresolved += 1
            else:
                print(f"RECOVERED {label}")
    return 1 if unresolved else 0


def _split_sources(values: Sequence[str]) -> set[str]:
    return {item for value in values for item in value.split(",") if item}


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--data-root", type=Path, default=Path("/training_data/climate_data"))
    parser.add_argument("--runner", type=Path, default=Path("/home/zhangmingyu/operation/download_run.sh"))
    parser.add_argument("--log-dir", type=Path, default=Path("/home/zhangmingyu/operation/logs"))
    parser.add_argument("--lock", type=Path, default=Path("/home/zhangmingyu/operation/lock/reconcile_sources.lock"))
    parser.add_argument("--now", help="fixed ISO-8601 UTC timestamp for validation")
    parser.add_argument("--only-source", action="append", default=[])
    parser.add_argument("--exclude-source", action="append", default=[])
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--verify-boundaries",
        action="store_true",
        help="also read each raw file's GRIB/7777 markers (manual deep check)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    only = _split_sources(args.only_source)
    excluded = _split_sources(args.exclude_source)
    policies = _selected_policies(only, excluded)
    unknown = (only | excluded) - {policy.source for policy in POLICIES}
    if unknown:
        parser.error(f"unknown source(s): {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")

    args.lock.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with args.lock.open("a+") as lock_handle:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(lock_handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            print("SKIP reconcile already running")
            return 0
        return reconcile(
            now=_parse_now(args.now),
            data_root=args.data_root,
            runner=args.runner,
            log_dir=args.log_dir,
            policies=policies,
            dry_run=args.dry_run,
            verify_boundaries=args.verify_boundaries,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Recover every production data path after the host/container becomes available.
set -uo pipefail

OPERATION_DIR="${OPERATION_DIR:-/home/zhangmingyu/operation}"
PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-/usr/bin/python3}"
DOCKER_BIN="${DOCKER_BIN:-/usr/bin/docker}"
CONTAINER="${CONTAINER:-zhangmy-dev}"
BOOT_LOG="${BOOT_LOG:-$OPERATION_DIR/logs/boot-recovery.log}"
BOOT_LOCK="${BOOT_LOCK:-$OPERATION_DIR/lock/boot-recovery.lock}"
WAIT_SECONDS="${WAIT_SECONDS:-300}"
WAIT_INTERVAL="${WAIT_INTERVAL:-10}"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$BOOT_LOG")" "$(dirname "$BOOT_LOCK")"
if [[ "${SKIP_LOCK:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
  exec 9>"$BOOT_LOCK"
  if ! flock -n 9; then
    exit 0
  fi
fi
exec >>"$BOOT_LOG" 2>&1

timestamp() { date -u '+%FT%TZ'; }
failures=0

run_step() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  echo "[$(timestamp)] START $label"
  if "$@"; then
    echo "[$(timestamp)] DONE  $label"
  else
    local rc=$?
    echo "[$(timestamp)] FAIL  $label rc=$rc"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
}

if [[ "${SKIP_CONTAINER_WAIT:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
  waited=0
  until [[ "$($DOCKER_BIN inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$CONTAINER" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]]; do
    if (( waited >= WAIT_SECONDS )); then
      echo "[$(timestamp)] container $CONTAINER unavailable after ${WAIT_SECONDS}s"
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep "$WAIT_INTERVAL"
    waited=$((waited + WAIT_INTERVAL))
  done
fi

# DWD is deliberately first: its per-cycle upstream window is only about 24 h.
run_step "DWD recent-init reconciliation" \
  "$PYTHON_BIN" "$OPERATION_DIR/reconcile_sources.py" --only-source dwd-icon

# Himawari commands are idempotent; their own realtime lock prevents overlap.
run_step "Himawari realtime catch-up" \
  /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/hima-realtime.sh"

run_step "remaining NWP recent-init reconciliation" \
  "$PYTHON_BIN" "$OPERATION_DIR/reconcile_sources.py" --exclude-source dwd-icon

run_step "Himawari recent-day rebuild" \
  env REBUILD_DAYS="${REBUILD_DAYS:-5}" \
  LOG="${HIMA_REBUILD_LOG:-$OPERATION_DIR/logs/hima-rebuild.log}" \
  /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/hima-rebuild-recent.sh"

run_step "GFS restore scan" \
  env SOURCE=gfs-0p25 /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/restore_scan.sh"
run_step "AIFS restore scan" \
  env SOURCE=aifs-single JOB=config/jobs/aifs_zarr_china.yaml \
  LOCK="$OPERATION_DIR/lock/restore_scan_aifs.lock" /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/restore_scan.sh"
run_step "IFS restore scan" \
  env SOURCE=ifs-hres JOB=config/jobs/ifs_zarr_china.yaml \
  LOCK="$OPERATION_DIR/lock/restore_scan_ifs.lock" /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/restore_scan.sh"
run_step "DWD restore scan" \
  env SOURCE=dwd-icon JOB=config/jobs/icon_zarr_china.yaml \
  LOCK="$OPERATION_DIR/lock/restore_scan_icon.lock" /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/restore_scan.sh"

run_step "ERA5 production reconciliation" \
  /bin/bash "$OPERATION_DIR/era5-production.sh"

echo "[$(timestamp)] boot recovery finished failures=$failures"
(( failures == 0 ))
